Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 113, verses 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

A'udhu: i.e., I seek refuge and protection.

Al-Falaq: i.e., the dawn.

Min sharri ma khalaq: from the evil of what He created, whether animate beings or inanimate things.

Ghasiqin idha waqab: i.e., the night when it grows dark, or the moon when it sets.

Al-naffathat: i.e., the female sorcerers who blow (on knots).

Fi al-'uqad: i.e., into the knots that they tie.

Hasid idha hasad: i.e., when he displays his envy and acts upon it.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾. It is reported that when Labid ibn al-A'sam, a Jew in Madinah, bewitched the Prophet (ﷺ), Allah, may He be exalted, sent down the two protective surahs, and Jibril recited them over him, and Allah healed him. For this reason, the two surahs are Madinan. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak﴾ means: Say, O our Messenger, "I seek refuge and protection in the Lord of the daybreak," who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for He is the one who splits the dawn and splits the grain and the date-stone, and none can do that except Him, owing to His great power and vast knowledge.

﴿From the evil of what He has created﴾ means: from the evil of what Allah, may He be exalted, has created of beings, such as accountable humans and non-accountable animals, and of inanimate things; that is, from the evil of every evil-doer among them and among all other created beings.

His saying, ﴿And from the evil of the darkness when it overspreads﴾ means: the night when it grows dark, and the moon when it sets, for darkness, whether by the coming of night or the setting of the moon, is the time when venomous snakes, beasts of prey, and groups of thieves emerge to rob, seeking evil and corruption.

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And from the evil of the blowers in knots﴾ means: and seek refuge with Allah, the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of the female sorcerers, who blow over every knot they tie and recite spells upon it. Nafth is the expelling of air from the mouth without saliva. For this reason it is reported: whoever ties a knot and blows into it has practised sorcery.

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾ means: and seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak from the evil of an envier, that is, of people, when he envies, that is, when he displays his envy, so that he seeks to harm you, intends evil against you, or wishes you ill because of his envy of you. Envy is the removal of a blessing from the one envied, whether or not the envier wishes for its removal, and this is the worst kind of envy.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to seek refuge in Allah and to take shelter in His presence from every feared thing that a person cannot repel, whether because it is hidden or because he is unable to deal with it.

2- The prohibition of blowing into knots, for it is a form of sorcery. Sorcery is disbelief, and the prescribed punishment for a sorcerer is a strike with the sword.

3- The absolute prohibition of envy. It is a dangerous disease that moved the son of Adam to kill his brother and moved the brothers of Yusuf to plot against him.

4- Ghibta (admiring emulation) is not envy, according to the sound hadith: "There is no envy except in two cases," where the intended meaning is ghibta.
